title: A Uniform for the Letter
premise: In 1893, on a storm-battered Cornish headland, widowed lighthouse keeper Ivo Okafor receives a letter in the unmistakable hand of Captain Elias Vane — the man whose death Ivo witnessed seven years ago and whose secret he promised to keep. The letter asks Ivo to shelter a fugitive arriving by sea: Vane himself, now living under another name and branded a traitor for documents he once entrusted to Ivo's keeping. As naval investigators descend on the station and Ivo's late wife's brother arrives among them, Ivo must choose between the loyalty that has defined his mourning and the truth that could clear Vane's name at the cost of his own standing. In the final storm of the season, Ivo reveals what he has hidden, saves both men from the wrecking seas, and accepts exile from the light he loves, finding belonging not in a uniform or a tower but in the promise he finally keeps aloud.
about_author: Y. M. Kavanagh is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the Atlantic coast. Their fiction explores how ordinary people carry extraordinary secrets through long silences.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo Okafor's POV. Seven years into his widowhood, Ivo keeps the light with ritual precision, hiding a sealed oilskin packet beneath the lamp room floor. A supply boat brings mail, including one letter in a dead man's handwriting. The emotional beat is the crack in a carefully ordered grief.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Decoding the letter, Ivo learns Vane lives and will come ashore during the next dark moon. Flashbacks reveal their wartime friendship and the promise made over an apparently dying man. Ivo prepares the station, torn between dread and a shameful flicker of hope.

chapters.title: A Man Called Grey
chapters.summary: Alternating Ivo and newcomer POVs. Lieutenant Harrow of the Admiralty arrives ostensibly to inspect storm damage, accompanied by Margaret Vane's brother, Edmund, who suspects Ivo knows more than he says. The beat is surveillance disguised as courtesy; every kindness becomes a test.

chapters.title: The Dark Moon Landing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In fog and heavy swell, Ivo rows out to meet a dinghy carrying a gaunt, bearded stranger who is unmistakably Elias Vane. Their reunion is cold with guilt — Vane blames Ivo for abandoning him that night. Ivo hides him in the disused oil store, and the lie begins.

chapters.title: Three at Table
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Hidden yards from his hunters, Vane endures the torment of hearing Edmund mourn him across the dinner table while Ivo lies smoothly. Vane wrestles with whether his return is justice or selfishness, and whether Ivo's silence is loyalty or cowardice.

chapters.title: Edmund's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Going through his sister's letters to Ivo, Edmund finds gaps — pages removed, dates mismatched — and confronts Ivo gently, offering friendship as leverage. The beat is intimacy weaponized: Edmund genuinely likes Ivo, which makes the suspicion unbearable.

chapters.title: The Packet Beneath the Lamp
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Harrow discovers the oil store disturbance and posts a watch. Ivo retrieves Vane's documents, reading them fully for the first time: proof Vane refused a convoy order to save civilians, twisted into treason. Ivo realizes the truth was never his to bury.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Water
chapters.summary: Vane and Ivo's alternating POV. Cornered by the tightening search, the two men finally speak plainly on the rocks at low tide — about the night Vane 'died,' about Ivo's wife, about what each owes the other. They plan to surrender the packet to Edmund, gambling on family love over institutional loyalty.

chapters.title: The Great Storm
chapters.summary: All POVs converge. As the season's worst gale strikes, the light fails mid-storm; Ivo must climb to relight it while Vane, exposed helping secure the boats, is seen by Harrow. Edmund reads the documents by lantern light as the sea tries to take everyone at once. Climax: truth and rescue happen in the same breath.

chapters.title: A Uniform for the Letter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, months later. Vane is cleared; Harrow is quietly reassigned; Edmund offers Ivo a home and a new post ashore. Ivo declines the reinstatement offered and leaves the tower he kept so faithfully, mailing one last letter — to his dead wife — telling her the whole truth at last. Resolution: belonging chosen, not assigned.
